ai.headline: MIT Schwarzman College of Computing launches pilot to help educators teach AI across disciplines

Inspired by MIT class C01/C51 (Modeling with Machine Learning) , a course developed through the Common Ground for computing and AI education that focuses on helping students understand and apply foundational AI and machine learning concepts to problem-solving in their own disciplines, the workshop gave educators an opportunity to explore how its materials and teaching methods could be adapted for their classrooms. The firms "likely" acted with "Chinese government awareness" when extracting capabilities from US models, including variants of Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Grok, agencies said.

ai.headline: What OpenAI's latest controversy tells us about the future of math
ai.summary: A milestone wrapped in controversy: OpenAI claims to have solved one of mathematics' most prestigious unsolved problems, the Navier - Stokes existence and smoothness problem, but the announcement has been overshadowed by accusations that the company built on two researchers' work without crediting them. Math's uncomfortable new reality: OpenAI solved in days what two humans spent nearly a year on, deploying 10,000 simultaneous AI agents at a cost of millions - resources no academic mathematician could ever access, raising hard questions about who math's future actually belongs to. Something is lost when AI wins: As Terence Tao has warned, the messy, public process of human mathematicians failing and iterating is itself valuable - and when private companies solve problems in secret, that generative chaos disappears along with the answer.

ai.summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT will have to comply with tougher EU rules such as removing illegal content or face potential fines, the European Commission said on Monday, as Brussels grapples with how its existing digital regulation applies to rapidly evolving AI services. The Commission said the chatbot, social media forum Reddit, and gaming platform Roblox would be classified as so-called very large online platforms under the EU Digital Services Act, its landmark online safety regime. The designation means all three services will face additional obligations such as removing illegal content and protecting the privacy and security of minors and could face fines of up to 6 percent of their global revenue if they fail to comply.

Inspired by MIT class C01/C51 (Modeling with Machine Learning) , a course developed through the Common Ground for computing and AI education that focuses on helping students understand and apply foundational AI and machine learning concepts to problem-solving in their own disciplines, the workshop gave educators an opportunity to explore how its materials and teaching methods could be adapted for their classrooms. The firms "likely" acted with "Chinese government awareness" when extracting capabilities from US models, including variants of Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Grok, agencies said.

harvest.headline: What OpenAI's latest controversy tells us about the future of math
harvest.summary: A milestone wrapped in controversy: OpenAI claims to have solved one of mathematics' most prestigious unsolved problems, the Navier - Stokes existence and smoothness problem, but the announcement has been overshadowed by accusations that the company built on two researchers' work without crediting them. Math's uncomfortable new reality: OpenAI solved in days what two humans spent nearly a year on, deploying 10,000 simultaneous AI agents at a cost of millions - resources no academic mathematician could ever access, raising hard questions about who math's future actually belongs to. Something is lost when AI wins: As Terence Tao has warned, the messy, public process of human mathematicians failing and iterating is itself valuable - and when private companies solve problems in secret, that generative chaos disappears along with the answer.
